solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Heading over here inspires the French to make sport

indicators.note: to inspire can mean to breathe or infuse into, so the French article takes the heading into its middle

parts.note: le is the French masculine form of 'the'
this clue sits under the printed heading of its section of the puzzle, the word for the horizontal clues

explanation.surface: A French title over a page tempts its readers into taking up a sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading over here' is self-referential: it names the label printed above this clue's own section of the grid, not a word heading anywhere in particular.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacrosse is a team game played with netted sticks, so it is an example of a sport.

clue.text: Paying guest drops round for English book

indicators.note: the lodger word lets go of its round letter
the new letter stands in place of the dropped one

parts.note: a lodger pays to stay in someone's home
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A lodger stops in to pick up an English book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops round' looks like 'visits', but it means losing the O.
explanation.definitionFit: A ledger is an account book in which financial records are kept.

clue.text: Unfinished work Dickens filleted for collected notes

indicators.note: an unfinished word is missing its final letter

parts.note: a chore is a piece of work

indicators.note: a filleted fish has its inside removed, so only the word's outer letters are left

explanation.surface: An unfinished Dickens novel was cut down for an edition of collected writings.
explanation.definitionFit: A chord is several musical notes sounded together, a group of collected notes.

clue.text: Nosy celeb mingled offensively

indicators.note: mingled means mixed together, so these letters are shuffled into a new order

explanation.surface: A nosy celebrity mixed with the crowd in a rude way.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscenely means in an indecent or disgusting way, an adverb matching offensively.

clue.text: Tarts left in alarm — pursued by a couple of bishops?

indicators.note: being pursued means having something follow behind, so this piece comes after
the letter goes inside the word for alarm

parts.note: a scare is an alarm or fright
bishops are chess men, so a pair of them is two men

explanation.surface: Pastries left in a panic, chased by two churchmen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tarts' looks like pastries, but it is the old slang for promiscuous women.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlet woman is an old disapproving phrase for a promiscuous woman, as is tart in slang.

clue.text: Evil chap in charge is probing

indicators.note: something probing pushes into another thing, so the abbreviation goes inside the word for a man

parts.note: a chap is a male

explanation.surface: A wicked man running things is investigating someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Malice is ill will or wickedness, a noun synonym for evil.

clue.text: Scottish town where everything's on tap, but not in prime locations

parts.note: everything means all

indicators.note: the letters standing at the prime-numbered positions, the second, third and fifth, are removed

explanation.surface: A Scottish town where all comforts are on offer, though not in the best spots.
explanation.walkthrough: In ONTAP, positions 2, 3 and 5 (prime numbers) hold N, T and P; dropping them leaves O and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Alloa is a town in Clackmannanshire in central Scotland, on the River Forth.

clue.text: Disastrous run-in with Asian people

indicators.note: something disastrous is a wreck, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A disastrous run-in with some people from Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Iranians are the nationals of Iran, a people of western Asia.

clue.text: Notice promoting parking outside big house fits condition

indicators.note: the notice word sits around the big house
promoting moves something up, so the parking letter is moved earlier in the word

parts.note: to espy is to notice
a pile is a large stately house

explanation.surface: A sign for parking outside a mansion suits the situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'promoting' lifts the P one place forward in ESPY, giving EPSY, before the big house goes inside; 'fits' looks like a verb but belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Epilepsy is a neurological disorder marked by seizures, so a medical condition involving fits.

clue.text: Dreadful time anticipated 24hrs after entrance to rented property is changed

indicators.note: the entrance to a word is its opening letter, here the first letter of the property word
says that opening letter is swapped for another one

parts.note: rooms are what a lodger rents
a day is twenty-four hours

explanation.surface: A landlord dreads the day after the front door of a rented house gets new locks.
explanation.walkthrough: The R that begins ROOMS is changed to D, though the clue does not say which letter replaces it; the blogger raised the same point.
explanation.definitionFit: Doomsday is the day of final judgement, a feared day everyone expects to come.

clue.text: Some talk a little — it's a matter of chemistry

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone speaks briefly about a subject that is really a question of chemistry.
explanation.definitionFit: An alkali is a base soluble in water, a substance studied in chemistry.

clue.text: Slow-motion screening of Al Pacino tyre burst

indicators.note: a burst tyre is blown apart, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A film moment with Al Pacino's tyre exploding, shown slowly on screen.
explanation.definitionFit: An action replay shows a moment of sport again, often slowed down, on television.

clue.text: Invest with no right to maintain position long term

indicators.note: says the word is left lacking the named letter, which is dropped

parts.note: to endure is to last or persist for a long time

explanation.surface: Advice on investing when you have no right to stay put for long.
explanation.definitionFit: To endue is to endow or furnish someone with a quality, the old sense of invest.

clue.text: 50% cut to a Borgia musical making comeback profitable

indicators.note: cutting the eight-letter name by half keeps only its first four letters

parts.note: Lucrezia Borgia, the Renaissance noblewoman

indicators.note: a comeback is a return, so the show's name is read backwards

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical

explanation.surface: A musical about a Borgia is shortened and revived, and turns out profitable.
explanation.walkthrough: Half of LUCREZIA is LUCR; EVITA backwards is ATIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucrative describes something producing a great deal of profit or money.

clue.text: Position taken by FT about centrist Liberal society representing a county

indicators.note: a stance taken by the paper follows the paper's own pronoun, so that pronoun comes first

parts.note: a newspaper calls itself 'we' in its editorials, so the FT is we

indicators.note: the stance word goes around the centrist and Liberal letters

parts.note: a stand is a position or stance
mid is middle, the centre

explanation.surface: The Financial Times takes a political stance on a centrist Liberal group standing for a county.
explanation.walkthrough: WE + ST(MIDL)AND + S. 'Representing' is a link word to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The West Midlands is a metropolitan county of England, centred on Birmingham.

clue.text: Secrets & Lies shot, without constraints of scripts, in English city

indicators.note: shot means wrecked, so these letters are thrown about
says some letters are left out of the shuffled ones
a word's constraints are its bounding letters, the first and last

explanation.surface: The film Secrets & Lies was shot in an English city without the restrictions of scripts.
explanation.walkthrough: Secrets & Lies is a Mike Leigh film, famously improvised. Take the S and S from the ends of 'scripts' out of SECRETSLIES and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Leicester is a city in the East Midlands of England.

clue.text: Foundation for Eve's make-up?

parts.note: in Genesis Eve is made from a bone taken from Adam's side, which formed the base of her body

explanation.walkthrough: 'Foundation' and 'make-up' suggest cosmetics, but the make-up is Eve's bodily making in the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: A spare rib is a cut of pork ribs, and punningly Adam's surplus bone from which Eve was created.

clue.text: Enumeration error in note on cycling matters

indicators.note: in a down clue, being on something means sitting above it, so this piece comes first

parts.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: cycling sends the last letter round to the front

parts.note: counts are matters, as in charges on an indictment

explanation.surface: A mistake in a note about matters concerning cycling.
explanation.walkthrough: COUNTS with its final S moved to the front gives SCOUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscount is a wrong tally, a mistake made when counting.

clue.text: Lavatory tax of a kind suggested by advisors to the throne?

parts.note: a privy is an outdoor toilet
council tax is the British local property tax, so council suggests a kind of tax

explanation.surface: A tax on toilets proposed by the monarch's advisers.
explanation.walkthrough: Council tax is the British household tax paid to local government.
explanation.definitionFit: The Privy Council is the formal body of senior advisers to the British monarch.

clue.text: Getting on with a German article polarising Germans

indicators.note: polarising sends things to the two poles, so these letters go at either end of the article

parts.note: G is the international code for Germany, so two Germans are two Gs
ein is the German indefinite article

explanation.surface: A German article that divides opinion among Germans, with an elderly slant.
explanation.definitionFit: Ageing means growing old, as getting on does in the idiom for advancing years.

clue.text: Imp moving erratically out of bounds

indicators.note: the word's bounds are its first and last letters, which are dropped

parts.note: lurching is moving suddenly and unsteadily

explanation.surface: A mischievous child darting about where they are not allowed.
explanation.definitionFit: An urchin is a mischievous child, a rascal or scamp.

clue.text: Never once arranged to come back together

indicators.note: arranging puts things into a fresh order, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A meeting that was never fixed again, though people planned to gather once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To reconvene is to meet again after a break, gathering once more as a group.

clue.text: She's fastidious about everything at first

indicators.note: the fastidious word goes around the single letter

parts.note: nice can mean fussy or precise

indicators.note: take only the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A woman described as fussy about everything from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a female relative, so she is a fair stand-in for a sister's daughter.

clue.text: Keen to repel half-hearted music

indicators.note: repelling drives something back, so the word is read backwards
the word's heart is its doubled middle letter, and losing half of that heart drops one of the pair

parts.note: reggae is the Jamaican music

explanation.surface: Someone is keen to drive away music that sounds lacklustre.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping one of REGGAE's two Gs leaves REGAE, which backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Eager means keen or enthusiastic, an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Tool for cutting journey meets with resistance

parts.note: a route is the way a journey takes
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: A cutting tool on a trip runs into some opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: A router is a power tool that cuts grooves and hollows in wood.

clue.text: Uniform found by trawl could be brill

parts.note: flat means even or uniform
to fish is to trawl for something

explanation.surface: A uniform turned up in a fishing net, and it might be great.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brill' looks like slang for brilliant, but here it is the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The brill is a European fish of the turbot family, an example of a flatfish.

clue.text: Bread's capital with, say, this

indicators.note: a capital letter is the opening letter, so take the word's first letter

parts.note: to utter is to say

explanation.surface: A spread goes with bread, as people say.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also points to bread and butter, the standard pairing.
explanation.definitionFit: Butter is the dairy spread most commonly eaten with bread, as in the phrase bread and butter.

clue.text: Inside information from spa hotel exposes something in the water

parts.note: a hydro is a hotel offering spa treatments, originally a hydropathic establishment
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A spa hotel leaks secrets revealing something in its water supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inside information from spa hotel' reads as one idea, but it splits into two pieces, with 'from' and 'exposes' as links.
explanation.definitionFit: Water is H2O, so hydrogen is one of the elements present in every water molecule.
